paragraphs.title: The Declaration of War and Edom’s Arrogance

easy.explanation: The ambassador called the nations to rise up against Edom in battle.
easy.q: Against whom was an ambassador sent among the heathen?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.”
easy.q: How is Edom described among the heathen?

answers: In the clefts of the rock and in a high habitation
easy.explanation: Edom dwelt in rocky clefts and considered its habitation high.
easy.q: Where did Edom dwell?

answers: It trusted in its high habitation
It was the greatest of the nations
medium.explanation: Edom’s pride caused it to trust in its high and secure dwelling.
medium.q: Why did Edom think it could not be brought down?

medium.explanation: Edom’s proud heart deceived it into thinking it was secure.
medium.q: What does “the pride of thine heart” mean?

answers: The mountain would always protect Edom
The nations could never reach Edom
The LORD can bring down even those in the highest place
medium.explanation: Even if Edom exalted itself as an eagle, the LORD would bring it down.
medium.q: What does the contrast between Edom’s height and its being brought down teach?

answers: The war would make Edom greater
It emphasizes the fall of a nation that considered itself powerful
Edom asked the nations for help
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts Edom’s pride with its true position and coming downfall.
challenge.q: How does Edom’s being called “small” relate to the declaration of war?

answers: No height can protect anyone from the LORD’s judgment
Edom needed to leave its land
challenge.explanation: Each image shows that the LORD can bring Edom down from any height.
challenge.q: What idea is repeated by the images of the eagle, the stars, and the rocks?

answers: Pride and excessive confidence in its dwelling place
challenge.explanation: The pride of Edom’s heart and its confidence in its stronghold are central to the prophecy.
challenge.q: What is the main cause of Edom’s fall in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Complete Plunder and the Betrayal of Allies

answers: The work of thieves and grapegatherers
The building of a new city
easy.explanation: The passage compares Edom’s destruction with thieves and grapegatherers.
easy.q: To what does the prophet compare Edom’s destruction?

easy.explanation: The hidden things of Esau would be sought out and exposed.
easy.q: What would be exposed when Esau was searched out?

answers: The men of its confederacy and those at peace with it
easy.explanation: Edom’s allies and friends would deceive it and prevail against it.
easy.q: Who would deceive Edom?

answers: The thieves would leave everything behind
medium.explanation: Unlike ordinary grapegatherers, the destroyers would leave no remnant.
medium.q: Why is Edom’s destruction described as more complete than an ordinary robbery?

medium.explanation: The passage asks whether grapegatherers would not leave some grapes.
medium.q: What would grapegatherers normally leave behind?

answers: They would give it accurate information
They would deceive it and wound it from within
medium.explanation: Those who ate Edom’s bread would lay a wound under it.
medium.q: How would Edom’s allies contribute to its weakness?

answers: The destruction would affect only the fields
The destruction would reach hidden and valuable possessions
challenge.explanation: The prophet describes not only outward plunder but also the searching out of Edom’s hidden treasures.
challenge.q: What does the movement from thieves and grapegatherers to hidden things show?

answers: Plunder, exposure of treasures, betrayal by allies, and the defeat of strength
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from plunder to exposed possessions, betrayal, lost wisdom, and broken warriors.
challenge.q: What sequence describes Edom’s collapse?

answers: To show that every part of Edom’s defense would fail
To offer them a new covenant
challenge.explanation: The removal of wisdom and the dismay of the mighty show Edom’s complete collapse.
challenge.q: Why are both wise men and mighty men mentioned?

easy.explanation: The passage speaks of violence against Edom’s brother Jacob.
easy.q: Against whom was Edom’s violence committed?

answers: It stood on the other side
easy.explanation: Edom stood by while strangers entered Jerusalem and carried away its forces.
easy.q: What did Edom do when strangers carried away Jerusalem’s forces?

easy.explanation: Edom entered the gate and laid hands on the substance of Judah.
easy.q: What did Edom do to Judah’s possessions?

medium.explanation: Edom should not have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction.
medium.q: Which action did the prophet say Edom should not have taken?

answers: Waiting in the road to attack escaping people
medium.explanation: Edom stood in the crossway to cut off those who escaped.
medium.q: What does standing “in the crossway” mean in this passage?

answers: It only watched from a distance
It joined the attackers, took possessions, and attacked or surrendered survivors
medium.explanation: The passage describes Edom entering the gate, taking property, and cutting off or delivering up fugitives.
medium.q: How did Edom’s actions go beyond merely standing by?

answers: Because Edom did not participate in the conquest
Because it witnessed the disaster, failed to help, and joined the attackers
challenge.explanation: Edom’s indifference and cooperation during Judah’s disaster made it guilty.
challenge.q: Why is standing by considered part of Edom’s violence?

answers: Watching, rejoicing, entering, taking possessions, and attacking fugitives
Rescuing, defending, sharing, and making a covenant
challenge.explanation: The verses move from observing the disaster to direct and increasingly cruel actions.
challenge.q: What is the escalating order of Edom’s actions?

answers: They list the acts for which Edom would be judged
challenge.explanation: The warnings identify the sinful actions that brought judgment upon Edom.
challenge.q: How do the repeated warnings beginning with “thou shouldest not” relate to Edom’s punishment?

paragraphs.title: The Day of Judgment and the Return of Retribution

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen.”
easy.q: Upon whom is the day of the LORD near?

answers: As it had done to others
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee.”
easy.q: What would be done to Edom according to its deeds?

easy.explanation: The nations would drink continually and swallow down the judgment.
easy.q: What would the heathen drink?

answers: A person receives according to his deeds
Deeds have no connection with judgment
medium.explanation: The passage teaches that the reward for one’s actions returns upon one’s own head.
medium.q: What principle of retribution is taught here?

answers: The consequence or recompense due for one’s actions
medium.explanation: The reward here means the recompense that comes because of what Edom did.
medium.q: What does “thy reward” mean in this context?

answers: The heathen would enjoy a feast
The judgment experienced by Edom would extend to all nations
medium.explanation: The verse broadens the image of judgment from Edom to all the heathen.
medium.q: What is the significance of comparing Edom’s drinking with the drinking of the heathen?

answers: The one who celebrated another’s disaster would experience judgment and destruction
The mountain would become a plain
challenge.explanation: Edom’s treatment of others would return upon itself in the day of judgment.
challenge.q: What is the central reversal described in the passage?

answers: To portray the severe reception of judgment ending in disappearance
challenge.explanation: The language emphasizes the overwhelming and destructive nature of the judgment.
challenge.q: Why are the heathen said to drink and swallow down?

answers: The day of the LORD is when deeds are judged and repaid
The day of the LORD is a national festival
The day of the LORD is a time of commerce
challenge.explanation: The day of the LORD brings judgment in which actions receive their due recompense.
challenge.q: How are “the day of the LORD” and “as thou hast done” connected?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Deliverance and Victory Over Edom

easy.explanation: Mount Zion would have deliverance and would be holy.
easy.q: What would be found upon Mount Zion?

easy.explanation: The house of Jacob is compared to fire and the house of Joseph to flame.
easy.q: To what are the house of Jacob and the house of Joseph compared?

easy.explanation: The house of Esau is compared with stubble that fire consumes.
easy.q: To what is the house of Esau compared?

answers: The possessions of the house of Esau
medium.explanation: The house of Jacob would possess its possessions.
medium.q: What would the house of Jacob possess?

medium.explanation: Deliverance refers to those who are rescued and preserved.
medium.q: What does “deliverance” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: Fire and flame kindle against and devour the stubble.
medium.q: What would the fire and flame do to the stubble?

answers: Both Israel and Edom would disappear
Israel would be preserved in holiness while Edom would be consumed
challenge.explanation: The passage places Zion’s rescued remnant opposite the destruction of Esau.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between deliverance on Zion and the house of Esau emphasize?

answers: To portray the united strength of Israel
challenge.explanation: Jacob and Joseph together represent Israel as a consuming fire against Edom.
challenge.q: Why are both the house of Jacob and the house of Joseph mentioned?

answers: It emphasizes the certainty of the prophecy
It announces a covenant with Esau
challenge.explanation: The statement assures the reader that the promised destruction will certainly occur.
challenge.q: What does “for the LORD hath spoken it” add to the conclusion?

paragraphs.title: The Restoration of the Land to Israel’s Exiles

easy.explanation: The verse says, “they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau.”
easy.q: Who would possess Mount Esau?

easy.explanation: They of the plain would possess the Philistines.
easy.q: Who would possess the Philistines?

easy.explanation: The verse states that Benjamin would possess Gilead.
easy.q: What would Benjamin possess?

answers: A redistribution of regions to Israel
The abandonment of the whole land
medium.explanation: The verses list different regions that would be possessed by parts of Israel.
medium.q: What do these verses describe concerning the land at Israel’s restoration?

answers: People living away from their homeland
medium.explanation: The captivity refers to Israelites who were exiled from their land.
medium.q: What does “the captivity” refer to in these verses?

medium.explanation: The captivity of Jerusalem in Sepharad would possess the cities of the south.
medium.q: What would the captivity of Jerusalem possess?

answers: The restoration and expansion of Israel’s inheritance
The route of an enemy army
challenge.explanation: The list presents the return of territories to different parts of Israel.
challenge.q: What common idea is expressed by the list of regions?

answers: The rescued remnant not only survives but receives an inheritance
challenge.explanation: After deliverance, Israel’s exiles are promised actual possession of land.
challenge.q: How do these verses relate to the earlier promise of deliverance?

answers: Different parts of Israel would possess different regions
All these regions belonged to Edom
The tribes had no connection with the land
challenge.explanation: The verses connect various Israelite groups with particular restored territories.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the mention of Ephraim, Samaria, Benjamin, and Gilead?

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Kingship From Mount Zion

easy.explanation: The verse says, “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion.”
easy.q: From where would the saviours come up?

easy.explanation: The saviours would come to judge the mount of Esau.
easy.q: What would the saviours judge?

easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “the kingdom shall be the LORD’S.”
easy.q: To whom would the kingdom belong at the end of the book?

answers: To judge the mount of Esau
To lead the heathen in battle
medium.explanation: The saviours ascend Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau.
medium.q: What is the role of the saviours in this verse?

medium.explanation: Saviours are those who bring deliverance.
medium.q: What does “saviours” mean in this context?

answers: It presents the purpose of judgment and deliverance: the kingdom belongs to the LORD
It announces that Edom will rule
medium.explanation: After Edom’s judgment and Israel’s restoration, the LORD alone possesses the kingdom.
medium.q: How does the final statement relate to the whole prophecy of Obadiah?

answers: Redemption ends in merely human political order
Deliverance leads to recognition of the LORD’s rule over all
challenge.explanation: The conclusion connects Israel’s restoration and Edom’s judgment with the universal kingship of the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the movement from Israel’s deliverance to the LORD’s kingdom?

answers: To emphasize Zion as the place of deliverance and holiness
challenge.explanation: Zion has already been presented as the place of deliverance and holiness.
challenge.q: Why do the saviours come from Mount Zion?

answers: Judgment of Esau followed by the LORD’s kingship
The fall of Zion followed by the rise of Edom
Harvest followed by the building of fortresses
challenge.explanation: The final verse summarizes judgment upon Edom and the ultimate establishment of the LORD’s kingdom.
challenge.q: What is the structure of the chapter’s conclusion?
